knowledge_point.title: Classifying a System as Consistent Dependent, Consistent Independent, or Inconsistent

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x+2y &=-3 \\ -6x-4y &=6,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is consistent independent

II. The system is consistent dependent

III. The system has no solution
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find the solution to the system. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x+2y &=-3 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
3x+2y=-3
$$

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, only statement II is true.
